detailed_description: The Text to Slug tool turns a title or phrase into a URL-friendly slug. It lowercases text, removes unsupported characters, converts spaces and separators into hyphens, trims extra hyphens, and updates the result on the page. It is useful for blog URLs, documentation anchors, product handles, and file naming drafts. Review generated slugs before publishing because project routing rules, duplicate URLs, and non-Latin transliteration requirements can differ.
usage_steps: Enter the title or phrase you want to slugify.
Adjust the source text if the slug is too long or unclear.
Copy the slug when it fits your URL style.
Check for duplicate slugs in your CMS or router.
Use the final slug in your page, article, or file path.
usage_examples: Create a documentation anchor from a section heading.
Draft a product handle for a catalog URL.
Normalize a file name for a static page.

faqs.question: What characters are kept?
faqs.answer: The generated slug keeps URL-friendly letters, numbers, and hyphen separators after normalization.

faqs.question: Does it guarantee a unique URL?
faqs.answer: No. You still need to check your CMS or application for duplicate slugs.

faqs.question: Can it transliterate every language?
faqs.answer: No. Non-Latin handling depends on the page normalization rules and may require manual review.

faqs.question: Should slugs be short?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Short, descriptive slugs are easier to read and share.

faqs.question: Can I copy the slug?
faqs.answer: Yes. The page includes a copy action for the generated slug.
